Hand fixture: 3 nodes, NodeRule [0,1,0]; edges 0->1 delay 0 weight 4 and 1->2 delay 1 weight 2; dt = ln 2, log_tau = 0, tau_syn = 1 (lambda = alpha = kappa = 0.5 exactly); theta_min 0, theta_max 2, theta_raw 0 (theta_base = 1 exactly); v_reset -1, refractory 1; external input [4,0,0,0] on node 0 only.
observed_result: The by-type mixed core is implemented in dynamics (NewMixed, MixedConfig, MixedParameters, MixedState, Forward, Backward, NewState, ValidateState, Advance, AdvanceModulated), wired into learning as the third coreModel with its own individual profile and neural-union member, and accepted by the checkpoint neural-union walk. 51 dynamics, 19 learning and 11 checkpoint mixed test cases pass, together with the whole existing suite. Hand computed 3-node table (continuous -> LIF -> continuous, one delay 1 edge), expected and actual identical to 1e-12: step 1 v=[2,0,0] out=[tanh 2,0,0] events=[0,0,0]; step 2 v=[1,-1,0] out=[tanh 1,1,0] events=[0,1,0] (node 1 candidate 2*tanh 2 = 1.9280551601516338 >= 1, resets to v_reset and starts one refractory step); step 3 v=[0.5,-1,0] out=[tanh 0.5,0.5,0] events=[0,0,0] (node 1 holds v_reset and ignores its drive, its trace decays to 0.5); step 4 v=[0.25,-0.5+2*tanh 0.5 = 0.4242343145200196,1] out=[tanh 0.25,0.25,tanh 1] events=[0,0,0] (the delay 1 edge finally carries x_1(2) = 1, so node 2 receives drive 2 and reaches v = 1). Advancing the same fixture as one call and as 2+2 calls gives bit-identical outputs, events and both state halves. No double counting: one LIF node feeding a continuous target (weight 2) and a LIF target (weight 3), both delay 0, delivers exactly w*x once to each; hand computed drives 0/0, then 2/3, then 1/1.5, matching the measured voltages [-1,0,0], [-0.5,1,-1], [-0.25,1,0.25] and the single event at the LIF target. Order independence: a 4-node, 5-edge fixture with two LIF nodes renumbered by the permutation 0->1, 1->3, 2->0, 3->2 (NodeRule, bias, log_tau, initial voltage and input rows permuted, theta_raw reordered into the new ascending LIF order, edge order unchanged) reproduces every per-node output, event and voltage bit for bit. Hand computed two-step gradient on the 3-node graph with upstream [[.3,-.2,.5],[.7,.4,-.6]] matches the declared rules to 1e-12 in all seven groups, including the exactly-zero second weight, which is the delayed LIF->continuous edge reading only the zero synaptic prehistory within two steps.

bit_identity.all_continuous_vs_Continuous: Bit-identical in both the ordinary and the -race build, for tanh and for softplus: Forward outputs, final voltage, all five Backward arrays (weights, bias, log_tau, inputs, initial; theta_raw is empty), and Advance outputs, step count, voltage and history. The state's ConfigHash necessarily differs, because a MixedConfig is a different document from a Config; the numeric state is identical.
bit_identity.all_lif_vs_LIF: Bit-identical in the ordinary build for Forward outputs, events and voltages, all six Backward arrays, and Advance outputs, events, voltage, history, adaptation, refractory counters, rate and homeostasis, in three variants (plain, adaptation, adaptation + homeostasis). Under -race the events, adaptation, slow stabiliser, refractory counters and every structural field stay bit-identical, while the membrane-derived values (voltage, synaptic trace, gradients) differ by at most 1e-16 relative to 1+|want|, which is below one adjacent float64 value at unit scale; the largest absolute deviation the fixtures produce is 1.39e-17, measured by lowering the tolerance constant until the comparison failed.
bit_identity.why_the_race_build_differs: This is a property of the existing spiking core, not of the mixed core. Go may evaluate lambda*v + alpha*drive with a fused multiply-add, which rounds once instead of twice, and the compiler decides that per basic block. TestMixedMembraneContraction measures it on the reference cores' own operands and fails if the recorded answer changes: Continuous.Forward fuses in both builds, LIF.Forward fuses in an ordinary build and does not fuse under -race, so LIF.Forward's own output moves by one adjacent float64 value between the two builds. The mixed core puts that one line in its own //go:noinline membrane function so its rounding is decided once and never by the surrounding code, which is why it matches Continuous in both builds. The build-tagged constants in dynamics/mixed_contraction_default_test.go and dynamics/mixed_contraction_race_test.go select exact comparison or the 1e-16 bound, and TestMixedMembraneContraction refuses to pass if those constants stop describing the build they were compiled into.

gradient_check: Two checks, both within what ticket 11 allows. (1) Central finite differences against the package-private smooth reference mode on a mixed graph (4 nodes, NodeRule [0,1,0,1], 6 edges with delays 0/1/2, adaptation enabled, 6 steps, tanh on the continuous half): weights, bias, log_tau, theta_raw, the initial voltage and every input row, eps 1e-5, accepted when the difference is at most 1e-4 relative or 1e-7 absolute. Every smooth spike was verified to lie strictly inside (0,1) and every continuous node's event entry to be exactly zero, so the differentiated model really is the smooth one. This covers both cross-type directions. (2) A hand computed two-step gradient of the hard-event model on the 3-node fixture, derived from the declared rules and compared to 1e-12 (the table is in docs/tickets/25-...md). Hard events are never finite differenced. The all-continuous assignment's gradient is additionally pinned bit for bit to Continuous.Backward, which has its own existing central-difference test.
learning_and_checkpoint: learning.Config.Mixed is three-way exclusive with Dynamics and LIF (none and more than one are both refused). The individual profile is mixed-f64-insyra-f32-persistent-inference-episode-learning/v1; NeuralState gains a Mixed member and every core refuses a state that carries a second half. Parameters.ThetaRaw has one entry per LIF node; the index map is published as Config().LIFIndex, is refused on the other two cores, and is refused when it contradicts the rule assignment. Trainable.Theta covers only those entries, and Options.Masks.Nodes reaches them through LIFIndex (masking the LIF node freezes its theta entry; masking only the continuous nodes leaves it updatable), checked both on the flat AdamW mask and through a real TrainEpisode. Local plasticity uses pre = out for every node, post = the 0/1 event on a LIF target and post = the output on a continuous target; a four-step hand computed eligibility with a closed gate pins both choices at the two steps that discriminate them. A gate that is actually open moves the fast state and leaves Parameters bit-identical. stdp_pair is refused on the mixed core because a continuous node has no event at either end of an edge. checkpoint.SaveIndividual/LoadIndividual round-trip a mixed individual including the node map and the slow stabiliser state, and refuse eight malformed union documents (two halves, wrong core, missing half, a configuration declaring two cores, and the cross combinations).
assumption_statement: Everything here is fixture scale and engineering-declared. The rule assignment (which neuron follows which rule) is a research declaration supplied in the configuration; nothing in this ticket derives it from the connectome, from cell type or from any published measurement. Whole-brain uniform mixing is not a default and is not supported by any experiment in this repository (main specification 2.1 D11). The numeric constants of the fixtures (dt = ln 2, tau = tau_syn = 1, theta_min 0, theta_max 2, v_reset -1, surrogate scale 1 or 2) were chosen so that every coefficient is exactly representable and the arithmetic can be checked by hand; they are not biological parameters. The fast_sigmoid surrogate is a declared approximation of the hard event, not the derivative of a real firing function.

limitations: No finite differences across hard events. The hard 0/1 event is not differentiated numerically anywhere; the surrogate is verified through the package-private smooth mode and through a hand computed gradient, exactly as ticket 11 requires.

Fixture scale only. The largest model tested here has 4 nodes and 6 edges. Nothing in this record says anything about whole-brain memory, wall-clock time or numerical behaviour at 165,122 nodes, and no real connectome or derived parameter set was used.
Vector nodes and shared parameters are stage two (COR-06) and recompute is stage three (LRN-02). Neither is implemented or measured here.

The all-LIF bit identity is exact only in an ordinary build. Under -race the membrane-derived values agree to 1e-16 relative rather than bit for bit, because LIF.Forward's own fused-multiply-add choice changes between the two builds. See bit_identity.why_the_race_build_differs; this is a property of the existing core and is recorded, not worked around.

checkpoint.ModelPackage does not carry the mixed core. Its topology fingerprint reads only the continuous and the spiking configuration, and the base64 node_rule array does not survive its required-field walk, so a mixed package would have been written with a fingerprint claiming no nodes and no edges and could not be read back. canonicalModelPackage now refuses it with a specific error and points at the persistent individual snapshot. Supporting it belongs to whoever extends the package format.
The simulate package's native runner does not offer the mixed core; it still selects one rule for the whole model.

stdp_pair is refused on the mixed core. A continuous node produces no event, and treating its absent event as "never fired" would be a silent wrong answer, so the rule is rejected rather than approximated.

The mixed state's ConfigHash is the mixed configuration's fingerprint, so a single-rule assignment's state half is numerically identical to the corresponding single-rule state but does not carry that core's hash. A mixed state is deliberately not loadable as a Continuous or LIF state.

Chemistry on a mixed individual is exercised only through the Modulation hook of the core (neutral modulation is bit-identical, a threshold entry on a continuous node is refused, a threshold entry on a LIF node suppresses its event). No end-to-end chemical fixture was added for the mixed core in this stage.

One machine, one Go version, one architecture: go1.26.5 darwin/arm64. The contraction behaviour recorded above is measured there; the build-tagged constant will fail the contraction test rather than silently mislead if another toolchain chooses differently.
